title: Trapping Rain Water
space_complexity: O(n) as submitted; O(1) achievable BOTH by squeezing my own approach (running segment-sum scalar) and via the canonical running-max two-pointer
revisit_reason: Solved with an original prefix-sum approach at O(n) space. Two follow-ups: (1) re-derive the O(1) squeeze of my own approach — the prefix arrays collapse to one running scalar; (2) implement the canonical O(1) running-max two-pointer, which is the version interviewers expect. Key lesson: the squeeze beat the 'creative leap' at zero asymptotic cost.
takeaways: The 'min of maxes' concept is fundamental for water trapping problems.
Dynamic Programming can be used to pre-compute maximums to the left and right.
An optimized two-pointer approach can solve the problem in O(1) space by maintaining `max_left` and `max_right` dynamically.
Monotonic stack is an alternative approach that can find bounding walls for each potential 'pit' efficiently.
Trapping decomposes as rectangle minus solid bars, and the solid-bar term is a range sum, so prefix sums genuinely help here (the mirror of why they failed on Container With Most Water).
The strict/non-strict (<= vs <) asymmetry between the two directional passes counts water bounded by equal-height walls exactly once.
C++ gotchas: 'continue' is a statement and cannot follow the comma operator; a single declaration cannot mix types (int i = 0, ll sum = 0 is illegal).
